newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures ended lower after a quiet session. September closed at $1,168, down from $1,670 and November closed at $1,622, down from $1,635 per tonne on Friday. The US market was closed for the Labour Day holiday but in London there was considerable nervousness over a substantial buildup in US fund long positions. It is feared that this could spark a sharp sell-off in New York on Tuesday.

COSTA RICA - Many in the coffee industry believe that the fall in coffee prices last year was the result of deliberate market manipulation and speculation. Now the president of Costa Rica's Coffee Institute called for the establishment of a minimum world coffee price to counter speculators in the world market. Alonso Lara, speaking at a meeting of the CEV group of Latin American coffee producers in Quito said that if no minimum price is set, speculators are going to continue taking advantage of countries that fix export quotas. Lara said it was vital for major producers in Brazil and Colombia to agree on policies to restrict exports and put a brake on speculation. He added that the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) has the faculties to take any measures to regulate supply. However, that is easier said than done, and the fact that the ACPC has no instruments to police the scheme is evidence enough that it is almost impossible to regulate supplies.

UNITED STATES - For the week ended August 24, coffee roastings in the United States totalled approximately 340,000 60-kg bags, down from 350,000 bags in the previous week and compared with 340,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 11.051 million bags, vs 10.770 million bags in the same year-ago period, it was added.

AUSTRALIA - Australia imported 70,038 bags of coffee in June 1996, 6 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 456,900 bags, 10 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 reached 814,700 bags, 7 per cent less than was imported the previous year. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Vietnam (126,000 vs 96,700 bags) and Papua/New Guinea (128,000 vs 99,000 bags).
